A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same temporal scaling-law research, with readable text, equations, figures, and tables. All 12 pages of v1 and 16 pages of v2 support comparison. v2 includes Appendices A–B; v1 ends with references despite mentioning an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM pre-training experiments, token-position loss fits, future-loss predictions, and benchmark evaluations of position-based loss weighting.

after.justification: v2 retains original fitting, prediction, and weighting results and adds experiments evaluating data-mixture selection, with further results in the appendices.

M1.justification: v2 introduces a two-stage data-mixture selection procedure: retrieve five candidates using a 58M model, then rerank them using predicted final losses after limited target-model training (Section 4). It also replaces v1's fixed fractional separation point with a derivative-threshold estimate (Sections 3.3–3.4). The underlying reciprocal curve family, renamed dynamic hyperbolic-law, is retained.

E1.justification: The OOD evaluation corpus changes from concatenated PG-19 validation/test data to the C4 RealNews-Like validation split (Section 3.2). LAMBADA is also removed from the downstream evaluation suite. Pile training, Pile validation, and the other seven downstream benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: v2 adds small-model selection and selection by actual loss after 10B tokens as evaluated comparators for its new pipeline; these select the same candidate and share result rows in Tables 2–3. Table 1 also adds a power-law comparator to complete-trajectory fitting. The three forecasting baselines remain, with v1's 'Exponential' relabeled 'Power-Law'.

E3.justification: Reported warmup changes from 2,000 to 1,000 steps, and token suppression starts after the estimated separation point instead of explicitly after 100B tokens. The new selection experiment introduces a 58M screening model, five candidates, and 10B-token target-model trials before evaluating completed 400B-token training. These are reported protocol changes; they do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 Table 4 adds ID perplexity evidence to the retained head/body/tail suppression ablation. Figure 6 extends the token-position loss-decrease analysis to the 1.2B model, while showing only the 20–40B and 140–160B intervals instead of v1 Figure 4's seven intervals. The central question about uniform learning across positions remains unchanged.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix B.1 first specifies averaging numerical evaluations over the last five checkpoints. This adds statistical aggregation information, without establishing additional independent runs. Neither version reports seed variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds mixture-selection results, weighting perplexities, power-law fitting scores, and appendix fitting results. For example, Table 2 reports 1.2B pipeline ID/OOD perplexities of 7.50/10.17 versus 7.55/10.29 for its baselines. The proposed method's OOD fitting R2 changes from 0.9987/0.9995 to 0.9983/0.9993 for 468M/1.2B, but the OOD dataset also changes. All 56 retained weighting benchmark averages match exactly; individual-shot and LAMBADA results are removed.

T1.justification: v2 Equation (7) introduces a formal derivative-threshold definition of the separation point, replacing v1's empirical fixed fraction. Equation (13) generalizes boundary conditions to all three fitted parameters. The principal curve forms and the derivation of position-independent loss derivatives remain, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: Hyperparameter selection changes from a prospective application in v1 to an explicit methodological and experimentally supported contribution in v2's abstract, introduction, and conclusion. The contribution statement now presents two use cases, including direct target-model selection. Claims about temporal loss prediction and uniform learning across token positions are retained.

C2.justification: v2 attributes late fluctuations in the loss-gap and sequence-scaling parameters to uncertainty at the first prediction position. It also interprets the new mixture-selection results as showing that small-model optima can provide useful candidates while remaining suboptimal for larger models. The interpretations of uniform token learning and the limitations concerning MoE architectures and transfer learning remain.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix B supplies architecture dimensions, head/layer counts, batch sizes, software versions, evaluation-harness access information, candidate-generation details, and loss-weight normalization. Section 3 newly specifies nonlinear least-squares fitting and residual-based outlier filtering/refitting. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation, although v1's explicit checkpoint interval of every 1B tokens is no longer specified.

R1.justification: v2 shortens the historical language-model and vision background and adds references including Switch Transformers, LLaMA 2, evaluation tooling, and time-series modeling. It more explicitly positions temporal scaling as complementary to existing model-size/data-scale laws and small-model hyperparameter tuning. The central scaling-law references and novelty positioning remain broadly consistent.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and method explanations are extensively rewritten. Prediction is organized into two explicit situations, the applications become separate use-case sections, much of the weighting discussion moves to Appendix B.3, and limitations receive a separate section. Terminology and model labels are standardized, including reciprocal/hyperbolic, IID/ID, and 1B/1.2B.

P2.justification: v2 adds application, perplexity, architecture, software, and strategy tables, plus appendix fitting plots. v1's large weighting table is condensed and moved to Appendix Table 8. The loss-decrease figure is redesigned from two panels with seven curves each to four panels with two curves each, and the forecasting figure moves later in the main text.

improvement.justification: v2 turns v1's prospective hyperparameter-selection application into a specified and tested procedure (Section 4, Tables 2–3), while Appendices A–B substantially improve methodological transparency and reproducibility. These resolve important gaps in practical validation and documentation. Removing LAMBADA and per-shot breakdowns reduces available evidence, and checkpoint averaging leaves independent-run uncertainty unresolved, but the gains in demonstrated applicability and inspectable methodology provide a substantial net improvement.
